subject: Hosted API tail latency spike — escalation & mitigation plan
messages:
From: Harrison Lowe <harrison@intellivatics.com>
To: rohan_mehta <rohan@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden p95/p99 latency spikes this morning

Rohan —

We started seeing severe tail latency (p95 up ~3x, p99 up ~6x) on hosted endpoints serving our customer-facing chat in us-west1 starting ~08:30 PDT. Some requests returned 500s; overall throughput dropped ~20% as retries kicked in. This is affecting our live demos for a partner event later today.

Can you confirm whether this is an infra or model change on your side? We haven't changed anything on our end. We need a short-term mitigation (rate limit reduction, fallback to smaller model) and an ETA for a fix.

Harrison
VP Product, Intellivatics
From: rohan_mehta <rohan@redwood.ai>
To: Harrison Lowe <harrison@intellivatics.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 09:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p95/p99 latency spikes this morning

Harrison — thank you for the heads up and I’m sorry for the disruption. We’re triaging right now. Short updates:

- We see the same tail amplification in our SLO dashboards for the hosted API in us-west1 (p99 increased from ~480ms to ~2.8s across several model variants).
- Error rate (5xx) rose from 0.2% to ~1.7% correlated with high allocation/retry cycles on a subset of GPU hosts.
- Immediate mitigation: we can enable auto-fallback to our smaller 'redwood-compact-v1' for queries from your API key — this will reduce latency at the cost of quality. Would you like us to flip that?

I’m looping in Laura (Customer Success) and Marcus (Runtime) to provide the ETA and a technical summary. We will keep you updated every hour until resolved.

— Rohan
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

From: marcus_lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, rohan_mehta <rohan@redwood.ai>, rachel_kim <rachel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p95/p99 latency spikes this morning

Team — preliminary findings from runtime traces:

- Symptom: periodic tail spikes and transient 500 errors on hosted API in us-west1 across nodes running A100-80GB instances.
- Runtime signals: accelerated allocation churn within the inference process; 'cudaMalloc' retries observed and GPU memory fragmentation counters are elevated.
- Crash/oom pattern: OOMs are not universal — they target worker processes that have higher cache footprints (long-conversation sessions). We also see KV cache growth beyond expected TTL in some pathways (suspect leak in cache eviction interaction with continuous batching).
- Short mitigation: rolling restart of affected worker pool + enable conservative KV cache eviction (kv_cache_eviction_threshold=0.65) and disable an experimental batching heuristic we rolled last week (batch_accumulator_v2=false).

I will start the rolling restarts now on a small canary set and monitor p99 — will report back in 20m. Attaching logs and a flamegraph from a repro session.

Marcus
Sr. Software Engineer, Runtime
Attachment: server_logs_uw1_0410.tar.gz

Subject: Re: Sudden p95/p99 latency spikes this morning

Harrison — we rolled a canary restart + enabled the conservative eviction policy. Early telemetry: p95 near baseline, p99 reduced by ~60% on canary nodes. No new 5xx observed from canary traffic.

Options:
- Keep fallback to redwood-compact-v1 for all traffic until full remediation (which buys time but reduces response quality).
- Gradually roll the runtime fix across the fleet (we expect full roll in ~3 hours if no regressions).

Your call on fallback. If you'd rather we avoid any model downgrade we can prioritise the full fleet rollout.

— Rohan

From: marcus_lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
To: rohan_mehta <rohan@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, rachel_kim <rachel@redwood.ai>, Harrison Lowe <harrison@intellivatics.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Final update: root cause and corrective actions

Harrison / team — final postmortem summary and next steps:

Root cause: an interaction between the new batch_accumulator_v2 heuristic and long-lived KV cache entries produced by conversational workloads. Under certain traffic shapes the heuristic kept batches open longer, increasing per-worker KV cache residency. That amplified fragmentation on 80GB A100 hosts and led to intermittent cuda allocation failures and process-level OOMs, which manifested as p99 latency spikes and transient 5xx.

What we did:
- Immediate: rolled back batch_accumulator_v2 across us-west1 and enabled conservative cache eviction; rolling restarts of affected pools completed within ~2.5 hours.
- Short-term: added a guardrail (kv_cache_resident_limit and aggressive eviction path) and a runtime metric that will alert before fragmentation reaches dangerous thresholds.
- Long-term: scheduler changes to limit long-conversation assignment to single-tenant worker pools and an upcoming patch to the allocator to reduce fragmentation impact (target release 2027-05-02).

Customer impact: Intellivatics saw p99 reduce to baseline and error rates return to normal. No data was exfiltrated and no requests were retried beyond normal bounds. We are offering a credit for the disruption to cover partner event risk (Laura will follow up on compensation).

Attachments: runtime-flamegraph-oom.svg, incident-timeline-20270413.xlsx

— Marcus
